text: [[selam]]! Today we read the life of one of the greatest saints of Ethiopia, [[tekle-haimanot]]. Read with me, then test yourself!
plain: Selam! Today we read the life of one of the greatest saints of Ethiopia, Tekle Haimanot. Read with me, then test yourself!

text: His parents, Tsega Ze-Ab (Gift of the Father) and Egzi-Haraya (Chosen by God), loved God and were kind to the sick and the poor.
plain: His parents, Tsega Ze-Ab (Gift of the Father) and Egzi-Haraya (Chosen by God), loved God and were kind to the sick and the poor.

text: On the twelfth of every month they kept the feast of [[kidus-mikael]] by feeding the poor. This is called a Zikir.
plain: On the twelfth of every month they kept the feast of Kidus Mikael by feeding the poor. This is called a Zikir.

text: In a vision, the Archangel told them they would have a blessed child, like John the Baptist. He was born on the twenty-fourth of Tahsas, and they named him Fesseha Tsion, the Joy of Zion.
plain: In a vision, the Archangel told them they would have a blessed child, like John the Baptist. He was born on the twenty-fourth of Tahsas, and they named him Fesseha Tsion, the Joy of Zion.

text: Three days after he was born, the Holy Spirit came upon him, and the baby spoke: One is the Holy Father, One is the Holy Son, One is the Holy Spirit!
plain: Three days after he was born, the Holy Spirit came upon him, and the baby spoke: One is the Holy Father, One is the Holy Son, One is the Holy Spirit!

text: Later there was a famine. His parents had little flour and oil left for their Zikir. Tap the jar.
plain: Later there was a famine. His parents had little flour and oil left for their Zikir. Tap the jar.

text: The young boy prayed, and the flour and oil grew, so the poor could still be fed!
plain: The young boy prayed, and the flour and oil grew, so the poor could still be fed!

text: He was ordained a deacon at fifteen. His parents wanted him to marry, but he wished to serve God.
plain: He was ordained a deacon at fifteen. His parents wanted him to marry, but he wished to serve God.

text: One day, while he was out hunting, the Archangel Michael appeared to him and said he would spend his life saving souls. He named him [[tekle-haimanot]], which means Tree of Faith.
plain: One day, while he was out hunting, the Archangel Michael appeared to him and said he would spend his life saving souls. He named him Tekle Haimanot, which means Tree of Faith.

text: He gave his money to the church and the poor, became a monk and a priest, and taught many people who did not know God. In Ketata, he drove out an evil spirit from a tree the people worshipped.

text: His monastery was on a high cliff, and the monks climbed up and down on a rope.

text: One day the rope broke! As he fell, he prayed to God. Tap the saint.
plain: One day the rope broke! As he fell, he prayed to God. Tap the saint.

text: [[selam]]! This year, every story we learn comes from one holy book. Let's find out what is inside the Holy Bible. Read with me, then test yourself!
plain: Selam! This year, every story we learn comes from one holy book. Let's find out what is inside the Holy Bible. Read with me, then test yourself!

text: The Bible is called holy because it was written by the inspiration of God. Holy men wrote it as the Holy Spirit moved them.

text: Everything we believe is based on the Holy Bible and on the holy Tradition of the Church. The stories we learn this year all come from it, or have their roots in it.

text: The Bible is not just one book. It is a collection of many holy books, such as Genesis, Isaiah, the Psalms, the Gospel of Matthew and the Book of Revelation.

text: The Holy Bible has two main parts: the Old Testament and the New Testament.
plain: The Holy Bible has two main parts: the Old Testament and the New Testament.

text: The Old Testament has the books written before the birth of Jesus Christ. In it we find the story of creation, the history of Israel and God's promise, the Ten Commandments, and prophecies about the coming of Christ.

text: The New Testament has the books written after the birth of Christ: the four Gospels about His life, the Acts of the Apostles, the letters (epistles) of the apostles, and the Book of Revelation.

text: Today we read a conversation between God and Abraham, about the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. It shows how much God loves the holy, and how He listens to their prayers.
plain: Today we read a conversation between God and Abraham, about the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. It shows how much God loves the holy, and how He listens to their prayers.

text: Read the story. Tap any paragraph if you would like me to read it to you.

text: Abraham was faithful and obedient to God. He was kind to the needy and welcomed strangers into his home, and God blessed him and was close to him.

text: God came to Abraham and said: Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do? The sins of Sodom and Gomorrah are very grievous, and I will destroy them.
plain: God came to Abraham and said: Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do? The sins of Sodom and Gomorrah are very grievous, and I will destroy them.

text: Abraham stood before the Lord and asked: Will You destroy the righteous with the wicked? If there are fifty righteous people in the city, will You not spare it for their sake? The Lord said: If I find fifty righteous, I will spare the whole place.
plain: Abraham stood before the Lord and asked: Will You destroy the righteous with the wicked? If there are fifty righteous people in the city, will You not spare it for their sake? The Lord said: If I find fifty righteous, I will spare the whole place.

text: Abraham kept asking, humbly, saying: I am but dust and ashes. What if there are forty-five? Forty? Thirty? Twenty? Each time the Lord said: I will not destroy it.
plain: Abraham kept asking, humbly, saying: I am but dust and ashes. What if there are forty-five? Forty? Thirty? Twenty? Each time the Lord said: I will not destroy it.

text: At last Abraham said: Let not the Lord be angry, I will speak only once more. What if ten are found there? The Lord said: I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.
plain: At last Abraham said: Let not the Lord be angry, I will speak only once more. What if ten are found there? The Lord said: I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.

text: But not even ten holy people lived in Sodom and Gomorrah, and the people never repented. The cities were destroyed by fire, and only Lot and his daughters were saved.
plain: But not even ten holy people lived in Sodom and Gomorrah, and the people never repented. The cities were destroyed by fire, and only Lot and his daughters were saved.
